label: General Relativity
author: Albert Einstein, 1915
description: General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass-energy, with dynamics governed by the Einstein field equations G_μν = 8πT_μν.

label: Quantum Mechanics (Copenhagen)
author: Bohr, Heisenberg, 1920s
description: The Copenhagen interpretation treats the wavefunction as encoding probabilities of measurement outcomes, with collapse upon observation as fundamental.

label: Schrödinger Equation
author: Erwin Schrödinger, 1926
description: The Schrödinger equation describes how the quantum state of a system evolves in time, serving as the fundamental dynamical equation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics.

label: Born Rule
author: Max Born, 1926
description: The Born rule states that the probability of a measurement outcome equals |⟨ψ|φ⟩|², connecting the abstract wavefunction to observable statistics.

label: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
author: Werner Heisenberg, 1927
description: The uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of physical properties cannot both be known precisely: ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2.

label: Second Law of Thermodynamics
author: Clausius, Boltzmann, 19th century
description: The second law states that entropy of isolated systems never decreases: dS/dt ≥ 0, providing the arrow of time and decay toward disorder.

label: Shannon Information Theory
author: Claude Shannon, 1948
description: Shannon's theory quantifies information as H = -Σp log p, establishing fundamental limits on data compression and reliable communication.

label: Standard Model of Particle Physics
author: Glashow, Weinberg, Salam, 1960s-70s
description: The Standard Model describes fundamental particles and forces (except gravity) via gauge symmetries SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1).

label: Many-Worlds Interpretation
author: Hugh Everett III, 1957
description: Many-worlds interprets quantum mechanics without collapse: all outcomes occur in branching parallel universes.

label: Wave Function Collapse
author: von Neumann, 1932; ongoing debate
description: The measurement problem asks how/why the superposition of states reduces to a definite outcome upon observation.

label: Participatory Anthropic Principle (PAP)
author: John A. Wheeler, 1970s–1980s
description: The participatory anthropic principle claims that observers do more than passively witness the universe; their acts of observation are essential to bringing physical phenomena into definite existence.

label: QBism (Fuchs)
author: Christopher A. Fuchs et al., 2000s
description: QBism interprets the quantum state as an agent's personal probability assignments about future experiences, treating quantum theory as a normative tool for updating beliefs.

label: Algorithmic Information Theory
author: Solomonoff, Kolmogorov, Chaitin, 1960s
description: AIT defines information content as the length of the shortest program that outputs an object, formalizing complexity, randomness, and Occam's razor.

label: Computational Universe (Lloyd)
author: Seth Lloyd, Schmidhuber, Zuse, 1960s–2000s
description: Models the universe as fundamentally computational, processing qubits via physical interactions with limits set by energy and spacetime.

label: Digital Physics (Zuse, Fredkin)
author: Konrad Zuse, Edward Fredkin, 1960s–1990s
description: Proposes physical reality is ultimately discrete and computable, like a cellular automaton updating binary states.

label: Principle of Least Action
author: Euler, Lagrange, Hamilton, historical
description: Physical systems follow paths that make the action functional stationary; reinterpreted as minimizing computational cost.

label: Unitarity in QM
author: Standard QM postulate, 20th century
description: Time evolution of closed systems is unitary (U†U = I), conserving probability and inner products.

label: Projection Postulate (von Neumann/Lüders)
author: von Neumann 1932; Lüders 1951
description: Measurement projects quantum state onto eigenstate corresponding to observed outcome.

label: Quantum Darwinism (Zurek)
author: Wojciech H. Zurek, 2000s
description: Classical reality emerges from quantum systems via selective proliferation of information about stable 'pointer states' into environment.

label: Klein-Gordon Field
author: Klein, Gordon, 1926
description: Relativistic wave equation for spin-0 scalar fields: (□ + m²)φ = 0.

label: Yukawa Coupling
author: Hideki Yukawa, 1935
description: Fermion-scalar coupling g·ψ̄φψ that generates particle masses after symmetry breaking.

label: Black Hole Information Paradox
author: Hawking, Bekenstein, Page, 1970s–1990s
description: Tension between unitarity (information conservation) and thermal Hawking radiation that seems to destroy information.

label: Planck Black-Body Law
author: Max Planck, 1900
description: Spectral distribution of black body radiation, resolving ultraviolet catastrophe via quantized energy.

label: Landauer's Principle
author: Rolf Landauer, 1961
description: Erasing one bit costs minimum energy kT ln 2, linking computation to thermodynamics.

label: Boltzmann Entropy
author: Ludwig Boltzmann, late 19th century
description: S = k_B ln W relates thermodynamic entropy to number of microstates.

label: ΛCDM Cosmology
author: Standard form 1990s–present
description: Standard cosmological model with cold dark matter and cosmological constant (dark energy).

label: Hubble Tension
author: Riess, Planck, 2010s–2020s
description: Discrepancy between local and CMB-derived Hubble constant measurements.

label: de Sitter Space
author: Willem de Sitter, early 20th century
description: Maximally symmetric solution with positive cosmological constant; model for exponentially expanding universe.

label: Baez-Stay Rosetta Stone
author: John C. Baez, Mike Stay, 2010
description: Uses monoidal categories to show structural parallels between quantum processes, topology, logic, and computation.

label: Infant Fairness Studies (Bloom)
author: Paul Bloom et al., 2000s–2010s
description: Infants show expectations about fair distribution and prefer fair agents before language develops.

label: fMRI Moral Judgment (Greene)
author: Joshua Greene et al., early 2000s
description: Personal moral dilemmas recruit emotional regions; impersonal ones engage controlled cognition.

label: Integrated Information Theory (Tononi)
author: Giulio Tononi, 2004–present
description: Consciousness = integrated information Φ; the whole has causal powers beyond its parts.

label: Orch OR (Penrose-Hameroff)
author: Penrose, Hameroff, 1990s–present
description: Consciousness from quantum computations in microtubules; collapse tied to spacetime geometry.

label: Global Workspace Theory
author: Baars, Dehaene, 1980s–present
description: Consciousness = global broadcast across distributed network enabling flexible access.

label: Bistable Attractors (Deco)
author: Gustavo Deco et al., 2000s–2020s
description: Resting-state brain as nonlinear system with metastable attractor states.

label: Bell's Theorem
author: John Stewart Bell, 1964
description: Proves no local hidden variable theory can reproduce all quantum predictions; reality is non-local.

label: Decoherence Theory
author: Zeh, Zurek, Joos, 1970s–1990s
description: Explains how classical behavior emerges from quantum systems via environment entanglement.

label: No-Cloning Theorem
author: Wootters, Zurek, Dieks, 1982
description: Quantum information cannot be perfectly copied; implies soul uniqueness.

label: Kochen-Specker Theorem
author: Kochen, Specker, 1967
description: QM is contextual: measurement outcomes depend on what else is measured.

label: Gleason's Theorem
author: Andrew Gleason, 1957
description: Born rule is the ONLY consistent probability assignment for quantum measurements.

label: EPR Paradox
author: Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen, 1935
description: Original argument for incompleteness of QM; led to Bell's theorem and entanglement research.

label: Bekenstein Bound
author: Jacob Bekenstein, 1981
description: Maximum information in a region is proportional to its surface area, not volume.

label: Chaos Theory / Strange Attractors
author: Lorenz, Mandelbrot, 1960s–1970s
description: Deterministic systems with sensitive dependence on initial conditions; strange attractors.

label: Gödel's Incompleteness
author: Kurt Gödel, 1931
description: Any consistent formal system rich enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove.

label: Church-Turing Thesis
author: Alonzo Church, Alan Turing, 1936
description: Any effectively computable function can be computed by a Turing machine.

label: Quantum Error Correction
author: Shor, Steane, 1990s
description: Protects quantum information from decoherence using redundancy and syndrome measurement.

label: Holevo Bound
author: Alexander Holevo, 1973
description: Upper bound on classical information extractable from quantum states.

label: Mutual Information
author: Shannon, 1948; extensions ongoing
description: Measures information shared between two variables: I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y).

label: Fisher Information
author: Ronald Fisher, 1920s
description: Measures precision of parameter estimation; connects to Cramér-Rao bound.

label: Epigenetics (methylation)
author: Various, mid-20th century onward
description: Epigenetic modification altering gene expression without changing DNA sequence.

label: Simulated Annealing
author: Kirkpatrick et al., 1983
description: Optimization via thermal annealing metaphor; escapes local minima.

label: Monte Carlo Methods
author: Ulam, von Neumann, 1940s
description: Numerical estimation via repeated random sampling.

label: Genetic Algorithms
author: John Holland, 1970s
description: Optimization mimicking natural selection: selection, crossover, mutation.

label: Bayesian Inference
author: Thomas Bayes, 18th century; modern 20th century
description: Updates probability as evidence arrives: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior.

label: Maximum Entropy Production
author: Prigogine and later, 20th century
description: Nonequilibrium systems maximize entropy production within constraints.

label: Constructal Law (Bejan)
author: Adrian Bejan, 1996–
description: Flow systems evolve to provide easier access to currents.

label: Causal Set Theory
author: Sorkin, Bombelli, 1980s–
description: Spacetime as discrete partially ordered set encoding causal structure.

label: Holographic Principle
author: 't Hooft, Susskind, 1990s
description: Information in region scales with boundary area, not volume.

label: AdS/CFT Correspondence
author: Juan Maldacena, 1997
description: Exact duality between bulk gravity and boundary CFT.

label: Loop Quantum Gravity
author: Ashtekar, Rovelli, Smolin, 1980s–
description: Background-independent quantum gravity; discrete area/volume spectra.

label: Twistor Theory (Penrose)
author: Roger Penrose, 1967–
description: Reformulates spacetime in twistor space; conformal geometry fundamental.

label: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
author: Multiple authors, 1990s–present
description: Beat-to-beat variation as index of autonomic/vagal balance.

label: Global Consciousness Project
author: Roger Nelson et al., late 1990s–
description: Worldwide REG network testing collective mind-matter interaction.

label: PEAR Lab Anomalies
author: Jahn, Dunne, 1979–2007
description: Decades of mind-machine interaction experiments with REGs.

label: Fractal Self-Similarity
author: Benoît Mandelbrot, 1970s–
description: Objects with self-similar structure across scales.

label: Scale-Invariant Geometry (Geesink & Meijer)
author: Geesink, Meijer, 2010s–
description: Coherent EM patterns repeating across biological/consciousness scales.

label: Solitonic Theory in 5D
author: Copinet et al., 2000s–
description: Stable localized wave packets in nonlinear systems.

label: Small-World Networks
author: Watts, Strogatz, 1998–
description: High clustering + short path length; efficient communication.

label: Predictive Processing
author: Friston, Clark, 2000s–
description: Brain as hierarchical prediction machine minimizing prediction error.

label: Active Inference
author: Karl Friston, 2010s–
description: Agents act to minimize expected free energy, not just update beliefs.

label: Hard Problem of Consciousness
author: David Chalmers, 1995
description: Why is there subjective experience? Why does information processing feel like something?

label: Mary's Room (Knowledge Argument)
author: Frank Jackson, 1982
description: Mary knows all physical facts about color but learns something new when she sees red.

label: Libet Experiments
author: Benjamin Libet, 1983
description: Readiness potential precedes conscious intention; challenges naive free will.

label: Default Mode Network
author: Raichle et al., 2001
description: Brain network active during rest, self-reflection, autobiographical memory.

label: Neural Binding Problem
author: Various, 20th century
description: How does the brain create unified experience from distributed processing?

label: Delayed Choice Quantum Eraser
author: Scully, Drühl, 1982; Kim et al., 2000
description: Future measurement choice affects past interference pattern.

label: Aspect Experiments
author: Alain Aspect, 1982
description: Confirmed Bell inequality violations; ruled out local hidden variables.

label: Split-Brain Studies
author: Sperry, Gazzaniga, 1960s–1980s
description: Severed corpus callosum creates two independent consciousnesses.

label: Fine-Tuning
author: Various, 20th century
description: Physical constants appear precisely tuned for life; 10^500 improbability.

label: Cosmological Argument (Kalam)
author: Al-Ghazali; Craig revival, 1979
description: Whatever begins to exist has a cause; universe began; therefore caused.

label: Gödel's Ontological Argument
author: Kurt Gödel, 1970 (posthumous)
description: Modal logic proof that a maximally great being necessarily exists.

label: Logos Theology (John 1)
author: John 1; Philo; Church Fathers
description: The Word (Logos) as divine reason/ordering principle incarnate in Christ.

label: Divine Simplicity
author: Aquinas, classical theism
description: God has no parts; all attributes identical with essence.

label: ER=EPR
author: Maldacena, Susskind, 2013
description: Entanglement (EPR) is equivalent to wormholes (Einstein-Rosen bridges).

label: Jaynes Maximum Entropy
author: E.T. Jaynes, 1957
description: Infer probability distribution maximizing entropy subject to constraints.

label: Fluctuation Theorems
author: Jarzynski 1997; Crooks 1999
description: Generalizes second law to fluctuating systems; entropy can decrease locally.

label: Szilard Engine
author: Leo Szilard, 1929
description: Showed information has thermodynamic value; resolved Maxwell's demon.

label: Margolus-Levitin Theorem
author: Margolus, Levitin, 1998
description: Fundamental speed limit on computation: π/2E operations per second max.

label: Self-Organized Criticality
author: Per Bak, 1987
description: Systems naturally evolve to critical states with power-law distributions.

label: Kuramoto Model
author: Yoshiki Kuramoto, 1975
description: Mathematical model of coupled oscillators synchronizing.

label: Autopoiesis
author: Maturana, Varela, 1970s
description: Self-creating, self-maintaining systems; definition of life.

label: Curry-Howard Correspondence
author: Curry 1934; Howard 1969
description: Proofs = Programs = Types; deep unity of logic and computation.

label: Tarski's Undefinability
author: Alfred Tarski, 1936
description: Truth predicate for a language cannot be defined within that language.

label: AWARE Study (Parnia)
author: Sam Parnia, 2014
description: Large-scale study of consciousness during cardiac arrest.

label: Aquinas Five Ways
author: Thomas Aquinas, 13th century
description: Classical arguments for God's existence from motion, causation, contingency, gradation, teleology.
